description: What the Projections workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs for a change. The `changes` job maps the changed files to their workspaces and crates and everything depending on them (tools/cli/src/lib/ci-facts.ts reads the graph), then applies these rules. See CONTRIBUTING.md#what-ci-runs.

full.description: Pushes to main, the nightly run, a manual run and the ci:full label run everything

files.description: CI itself, a toolchain, a lockfile or root manifest, or the repository's tooling: run everything
Markdown nothing reads, outside test data and templates, is documentation

Markdown a crate embeds or a generator reads or writes (help text, agent prompts, reference and built-in pages): the Linux checks, which run every crate's tests and generator's check, and not the jobs for what embeds it
A file in a workspace or crate is that workspace's or crate's change
A file a crate reads by path, or a generator reads or writes, is a change to what reads it
Documentation outside every workspace and crate
Configuration only the checks read (file standards, formatting, lint, the self-projection), the GitHub Action and the release configuration: the Linux checks, and what the tags select
A file no rule recognises: run everything, to be safe

os-specific.description: Rust, the GitHub Action and the CLI's packaging scripts: what macOS checks beyond Linux

actions-lock.description: The workflow dependency lockfile verifies upstream

browser.description: The browser suites: each workspace with a test:browser script. Those with shards run in their own jobs; every other affected suite runs in `browser (rest)`.

default.description: A suite runs when the change reaches it or a workspace its test:browser script builds

packages/renderers/harness.description: Every built-in renderer in the real host frame. It runs when what it tests changes (the renderers, the kit, the renderer SDK and protocol, the schemas and the Engine they use), not for the CLI's backend, which serves it fixtures. Shards are by measured time: about 64, 72, 40 and 70 test-minutes per project on two workers. macOS runs WebKit, the platform Safari runs on.

narrow.description: A change to some built-in renderers alone leaves the other renderers' tests out (--grep-invert)

packages/host/inspector.description: The Inspector, against the CLI's backend, exploring and extracting from repositories

examples/renderers/minimal.description: The minimal example renderer, against the CLI's backend in fixtures mode
